In this month our record shows us converging. Most of us — 44 — said "a government shutdown", a phrase John Cornyn first entered on 2013-01-04. 41 of us said "the debt ceiling", which Tom McClintock had first said years earlier. 38 of us said "keep the government".

Then, near the same peak, our language turned to a bill: 40 of us said "water resources reform", 39 said "the water resources", 38 said "the water resources reform", 35 said "and development act", and 34 of us said the full "water resources reform and development act" together.

We report this without comment. In one stretch we spoke of "a government shutdown" and "the debt ceiling"; in another we read the same bill's name aloud in near-unison. The record does not show us explaining the turn. It shows only that we made it, and how many of us made it at once.

top_phrases.phrase: water resources reform and development act
